Anthropic is poised to generate multibillion-dollar gains for its largest financial backers when its stock starts trading on the Nasdaq $NDAQ on Thursday, according to Bloomberg.

According to recent reports, the organization set a price of $83 a share on Wednesday, which puts its fully diluted market value at about $1.5 trillion. The stock will trade under the ticker ANT. The offering raised $81.3 billion, including stock sold by existing stockholders, the company mentioned.

According to recent reports, that total exceeds the $75 billion SpaceX raised at the start of its June IPO, according to NPR. SpaceX's total climbed to $85.7 billion once its underwriters took up the option to sell additional shares, according to CNBC.

It has been revealed that lightspeed Venture Partners has invested more than $3.5 billion in Anthropic since early 2024. Its stake comes to roughly $28 billion at the offering price, according to Bloomberg. ICONIQ has put in more than $6 billion, starting last year when Anthropic was valued at $183 billion, and its stake is worth over $26 billion. Menlo Ventures led the organization's Series D round in 2024 with $500 million, has invested more than $1 billion in total and holds a stake worth nearly $22 billion.

The stake values are estimates, and the dilutive effect of the new shares may not be factored in, according to Bloomberg. ICONIQ, Menlo and Lightspeed have placed orders for more shares in the offering, but the amounts they will be given have not been made public.

In a recent development, coatue Management has committed $4.75 billion to Anthropic over several funding rounds, including $2.5 billion in the February round and $2 billion in May at a $965 billion valuation. Its first investment was $250 million in 2025, in a round that valued Anthropic at $183 billion. At the IPO price, its stake is worth about $16 billion, according to Bloomberg.

Recent findings suggest that singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC has invested more than $4.5 billion and holds a stake worth about $15 billion. General Catalyst has put in about $2 billion for a stake worth around $10 billion. Bessemer Venture Partners has invested more than $800 million for a stake of about 0.5%, or $7.5 billion, according to Bloomberg.

Spark Capital invested $75 million in 2023, and its stake is worth about $11 billion, according to Bloomberg. An investment team that includes Guy Oseary, Ashton Kutcher and Sound Ventures managing partner Effie Epstein owns shares valued at close to $11 billion.

Recent findings suggest that former Google $GOOGL Chief Executive Officer Eric Schmidt, 71, backed Anthropic in 2021 with a check in the tens of millions, at a time when the manufacturer was valued at $461 million. His stake is projected to come to roughly $15 billion at the IPO valuation, according to Bloomberg.

After a $26 billion private placement with seven tech companies, Amazon $AMZN holds close to 15% of Anthropic's shares outstanding, while Google has roughly 14%, according to Bloomberg.

Why Microsoft is aiming to make Copilot the ‘OS for work’

💡 Key Takeaways

  • These days, Microsoft executives have likened Copilot to an operating system, or as CEO Satya Nadella called it, “a new OS for work.” This doesn’t mean Microsoft is replacing Windows with Copilot (even though there was a Microsoft incubation project, codenamed “Project Aion,” that focused on the idea of a “Copilot OS”).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Mary Jo Foley on Nov 16, 2026 at 5:44 amNovember 16, 2026 at 5:44 am.

Sources indicate that it’s been quite a while since Microsoft was “the Windows manufacturer,” meaning it derived the bulk of its revenues from Windows. However, Windows — along with Office — has helped Microsoft build a moat that has largely shielded it from forces that have battered some of its competitors as AI has risen to prominence.

These days, Microsoft executives have likened Copilot to an operating system, or as CEO Satya Nadella called it, “a new OS for work.” This doesn’t mean Microsoft is replacing Windows with Copilot (even though there was a Microsoft incubation project, codenamed “Project Aion,” that focused on the idea of a “Copilot OS”).

Plus, as the head of Windows discovered the hard way, many Windows users are dead set against Windows morphing into an “agentic OS.”.

Instead, the Copilot as “a new OS for work” descriptor is a metaphor, but one with considerable history and significance.

It has been revealed that microsoft is betting that the race to bring AI into the workplace will be won by whoever controls the layer underneath the models — the data, permissions, security and management tools that businesses already run on Microsoft software. That’s the job Windows has done for decades, and it’s the part of the AI business where Microsoft starts out ahead.

According to recent reports, many of the components behind the OS metaphor are likely to be on display at the firm’s annual Ignite conference in San Francisco this week. According to the session list for the weeklong event for customers and partners, Microsoft will highlight how Copilot acts as a platform for building, hosting and managing AI solutions.

Industry observers note that the high-level pitch: Copilot can do it all. It can be the foundational layer for your agents, applications, and business processes.

According to recent reports, operating systems like Windows provide users with a way to interact with their applications and resources via a common interface across software and data. They orchestrate under the covers what’s happening when users perform specific tasks.

Taking the metaphor to the extreme, if Copilot can be seen as the latest Windows, agents are the new apps; skills are the Win32 programming interfaces; and the Graph and IQ layers are like File Explorer.

The Newly introduced OS Metaphor: Why Now? For the past year-plus, Microsoft has been working to get customers to think about Copilot as not so much a chatbot, but more a full-stack platform. Its recently introduced Copilot “super app” is meant to be the unifying interface across this platform.

Industry observers note that at the moment, the new Copilot app provides customers with Code, Cowork and Autopilot access. But beneath that top layer, Microsoft is adding other integrations to its core Microsoft Office experiences, Microsoft IQ intelligence backends, its CRM and ERP Dynamics capabilities, and agents and applications from other vendors and customers, as well.

Microsoft’s inclusion of its core Office capabilities in the latest Copilot comes none too soon, as Anthropic last week introduced new Claude-based tools for spreadsheets and whiteboards, and previewed one for meetings, that compete more directly with Microsoft’s Office apps.

The “Copilot as Fresh OS” metaphor also works when you consider that Microsoft is looking to the new Copilot app to raise the level of abstraction, or hide the underlying complexities, of how agentic computing works.

It has been revealed that if you believe the AI story lines, we’re moving to a world where many customers expect to be able to ask a system to turn a bunch of slides into a business blueprint and then share that plan with a group of coworkers. In this scenario, customers don’t have to think about which apps and data sources they need to pull together to achieve this; they will count on their AI system to figure it out and just do it on their behalf.

“We increasingly think of all our apps together as a latest operating system for work that transcends traditional software categories to understand user intent and act on it,” said Nadella in his letter to shareholders, published as part of Microsoft’s annual report on Oct. 21.

Sources indicate that the end goal? “As our apps move toward agent-first capabilities that can be called and orchestrated in the flow of work, the system becomes more valuable and more deeply embedded,” Nadella noted.

In a recent development, the Slow and Unsexy Enterprise Race: In the enterprise space, being first and fastest doesn’t always win the race. While AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic vie to be the AI model kingmakers, Microsoft is content to focus on the less sexy but more difficult-to-deliver elements like context, permissions, skills, orchestration, governance and security, all hallmarks of operating systems like Windows.

Microsoft will try to pull all these OS-like pieces together at this week’s Ignite and show customers that it’s got what it takes with Copilot to make AI promises more than just demoware.

Cardano DReps have rejected a proposal by Toto Finance to spend 22 million ADA from the Cardano treasury on a "Strategic Copper Reserve.".

In a recent development, the vote closed on Nov. 15, and DReps holding 2.86 billion ADA voted against the proposal, according to Cardano governance data. DReps with 20.02 million ADA voted in favor of it.

DRep John MacPherson was among those who voted "No," and he explained his decision in a post on X.

It has been revealed that macPherson wrote that he is not against real-world assets on Cardano. Still, he said the proposal asks the treasury "to take on both the copper price and the ada price," and Toto Finance would collect "up to about 3.4M ada in fees.".

At the same time, MacPherson said that the proposal is “more honest about its risks than most.”.

Toto Finance, a tech giant led by Monty Metzger, submitted the proposal on Oct. 15. ADA is trading at $0.152 on Monday, and the requested 22 million ADA is now worth around $3.3 million.

Recent findings suggest that the initiative was to buy copper with 14.72 million ADA and store it in a warehouse near Fresh Orleans. Toto Finance wanted to issue one CuTT token for each pound of copper. The metal would be sold in 18 to 24 months.

The Cardano Foundation, which votes as a DRep, declared its "No" vote in October.

"We recognize the opportunity in real-world asset tokenization; however, this proposal places 22,000,000 ada under the recipient's sole control to fund a fee-heavy concentrated commodity position whose safeguards are not yet in place," the foundation wrote.

Three members of the Constitutional Committee voted "No," and the other four members did not vote.

In a recent development, crypto commentator Ingeniero Cripto agreed with MacPherson in the replies under his post. He called the "double exposure" to the prices of copper and ADA the key problem of the proposal, as the Cardano treasury already holds ADA.

According to him, RWAs on Cardano make sense, but “funding the asset itself is a different question than funding the rails.”.

Groundcover releases Agent Investigations, a shared workspace for AI agents and engineers

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that observability company groundcover Inc.
  • According to recent reports, agent Investigations is aimed at the problem of scattered findings as AI agents take on a bigger role in incident response.
  • Sources indicate that investigations in the newly introduced workspace are started automatically by groundcover once a monitor problem opens.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Sources indicate that observability company groundcover Inc. today unveiled the launch of Agent Investigations, a shared workspace designed to allow groundcover’s artificial intelligence agents, a team’s own coding agents and on-call engineers to work production incidents together.

According to recent reports, agent Investigations is aimed at the problem of scattered findings as AI agents take on a bigger role in incident response. When production goes down, several engineers often point their own agents at the same issue, with each agent working in isolation, according to the firm. What those agents conclude, it claims, is end up in private chats, tickets or Slack messages out of view of the rest of the team.

Sources indicate that investigations in the newly introduced workspace are started automatically by groundcover once a monitor problem opens. Engineers also have the option to launch one manually from the groundcover interface or from a button in Slack.

On groundcover’s side, the work is split between two agents. The first, known as the Investigator agent, is said to build a graph of questions and hypotheses before testing each one against groundcover’s logs, metrics, traces and Kubernetes data. Supporting graphs are attached to each of its findings.

Reviewing every proposed conclusion is the job of the second, a Moderator agent. The Moderator, which is the only agent allowed to close a hypothesis, sends back any claim that lacks supporting findings. Doing so is mentioned to separate generating a possible explanation from validating whether the evidence actually supports it.

Ending each hypothesis is a structured assessment that either supports or refutes it. The tech giant claims teams get a set of tested answers to read through instead of pages of generated text.

In a recent development, agent Investigations also offers access for outside agents, including Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code and OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex, through groundcover’s Model Context Protocol server. Connected agents can read from and contribute to the same investigation, with agents used for business intelligence and product roadmapping also able to take part. In October, groundcover introduced agent-to-agent observability tools that let outside coding agents hand production investigations to its own agent.

Hypothesis status and assessments post to the Slack thread tied to the original alert. With replies posted in that thread also fed back into the investigation, engineers are able to steer the work from inside the incident conversation.

It has been revealed that “Every engineer now has an agent, but each of those agents investigates on its own and findings end up in a chat window,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Shahar Azulay, who started groundcover in 2021 with Yechezkel Rabinovich. “Agent Investigations gives humans and agents one place to work an incident, where every hypothesis is tested against production data and every conclusion has to be backed by evidence.”.

Omer Mayer, senior product manager at groundcover, mentioned the wait while agents are working and the on-call engineer has nothing to look at is often “the hardest stretch of an incident.” Engineers using Agent Investigations instead get to watch, he said, as each hypothesis is supported or ruled out in real time.

Recent findings suggest that the graph the Investigator builds also serves as the record, said to show how a team reached the root cause, including the hypotheses that were ruled out along the way. According to the company, keeping the monitor, Slack thread, investigation and conclusion linked means nobody has to piece the history back together from separate tools after an incident closes.

Powering the investigations is the full-fidelity telemetry collected by groundcover’s sensor. Because groundcover uses a bring-your-own-cloud architecture, the data remains in the customer’s own cloud account even while agents are querying it.

Agent Investigations is available to groundcover customers whose backends have AI enabled. The manufacturer will demonstrate it at Amazon Web Services Inc.’s re:Invent conference in Las Vegas Nov. 30-Dec. 4.

Groundcover has raised $160 million to date, including a $100 million Series C round led by One Peak in July.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that zetaChain's Governance Proposal 2 would halt its L1 around Dec 9, mint ZETA 1:1 on Solana and burn about 55M ZETA in monthly installments.
  • Recent findings suggest that headlines are calling it a 55 million ZETA burn.
  • It has been revealed that zetaChain published Governance Proposal 2 on November 4, and its announcement post lays out the mechanics.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Recent findings suggest that zetaChain's Governance Proposal 2 would halt its L1 around Dec 9, mint ZETA 1:1 on Solana and burn about 55M ZETA in monthly installments. Voting closes Nov 7.

Recent findings suggest that headlines are calling it a 55 million ZETA burn. Read the proposal's own schedule, though, and nothing close to 55 million disappears on the day the chain halts. The figure is real, but it arrives in twelve installments over 2027.

It has been revealed that zetaChain published Governance Proposal 2 on November 4, and its announcement post lays out the mechanics. About 55 million ZETA of undistributed validator emissions will be burned monthly through 2027, following the schedule on which they would have been emitted. The roadmap in the same post puts the pace at twelve monthly burns of roughly 4.6 million ZETA each, from January to December 2027.

According to recent reports, that detail changes how the number should be read. Most of the early flash coverage collapsed it into a single burn, which implies an immediate supply shock. The staged schedule tells a different story. These tokens were never going to circulate, because they are validator rewards for an L1 that is about to stop. Burning them on the original emission timetable keeps the published release schedule intact and introduces no fresh mechanism, as ZetaChain's FAQ puts it.

In a recent development, governance Proposal 2 builds on Proposal 68, which approved the move to Solana in September with 99.4% in favor. Proposal 2 supplies the mechanics. Voting runs 72 hours and closes on November 7, and ZetaChain indicates nothing moves unless it passes.

If it does pass, every ZETA balance is recorded at snapshot block 20,755,000, expected around December 9. The ZetaChain L1 halts at that same height and isn't restarted. Claims open the same day through the ZetaHub migration portal, and ZetaChain's upcoming private AI app, ZetaLabs, launches alongside it.

The proposal also pairs the migration with a fresh whitepaper, which ZetaChain calls the document of record for the token after the move.

The snapshot goes well beyond a simple wallet count. It records liquid, staked, unbonding and unclaimed-reward balances. Staked ZETA is credited automatically, so nobody has to unstake, and exchange balances convert without any action from holders. Staking rewards stop at the snapshot height.

Recent findings suggest that holders who want to claim directly face a short process. They connect the wallet that held ZETA, sign a message naming a Solana wallet, and receive the full balance shortly afterward. The claim costs no fee and requires no SOL. According to the post, the portal asks only for a signature, never for a transaction or a seed phrase. A minimum of 10 ZETA at the snapshot is needed to claim.

Two edge cases deserve attention. First, ZETA wrapped or sitting in pools and contracts can't be claimed by a key, so holders need to unwrap and exit before the snapshot. Second, assets still held as ZRC-20 tokens at the snapshot can be claimed back on their original chain through a separate bridged-assets page, with a $5 minimum per token. Both are the kind of detail that catches people out when a deadline arrives.

According to recent reports, on Solana, ZETA becomes a native SPL token under the same ticker, with 9 decimals and no freeze authority. The full snapshot total is minted before the portal opens, and then the mint authority is revoked, so no one can ever mint more. No third-party bridge is involved.

According to recent reports, that sequence is the strongest holder protection in the proposal, and it is also the part that can be checked in public. The supply stays capped at 2.1 billion less whatever has been burned, and ZetaChain says it will publish the SPL mint address and the migration program address before December 9. Once those exist, anyone can compare the minted total against the snapshot and confirm that the authority was actually revoked. That confirmation deserves the most scrutiny.

Meanwhile, the portal and its program are under independent review by Hacken, and ZetaChain states the portal opens only after the review is complete and the report is published. The ERC-20 version of ZETA on Ethereum is unaffected by the proposal. Purchaser and core contributor vesting completes on January 1, 2027, and ZetaChain says no newly released ZETA will be sold in 2027.

The biggest practical risk is inattention. Most holders don't need to do anything until December 9, but exchange people depend on each exchange's own conversion window, and anyone holding ZETA through a contract or pool has homework to do beforehand.

Scams add another layer of risk. Any migration with a claim portal invites imitators, and ZetaChain tells holders to trust only its official domains and social accounts. A simple rule of thumb helps here: a site that asks for a seed phrase should be closed immediately, since the legitimate flow only needs a message signature.

In a recent development, on the technical side, claims are checked against the published snapshot rather than the live chain, so they continue to work after the halt. ZetaChain notes it will announce any change to the process in advance.

In a recent development, the vote decides the terms, not the direction. If Proposal 2 fails, the direction approved in Proposal 68 stands and ZetaChain returns with a revised proposal. Nothing moves on these terms.

If it passes, the sequence is clear. The security report, mint address and migration program address arrive before December 9. The snapshot, halt, mint and portal opening follow on the day, and the monthly burns run through 2027. ZetaLabs then adds a Premium tier in the first quarter of 2027, with ZETA as the token for access and payment.

Taken together, this looks more like a retirement strategy for an L1 than a dramatic supply event. The burn is gradual, the mint is capped, and the claim process is simple on paper. Execution is what will matter most: the audit report, the published addresses and the clean revocation of mint authority. Those are the items to watch between now and December 9.

HOUSTON, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Arkestro, the leading predictive procurement platform accelerating enterprise scale, today announced that Phillips 66 (NYSE: PSX) has formalized a long-term partnership to expand its use of Arkestro's predictive procurement platform following strong results from an initial deployment across refining, midstream, and lubricants operations.

In a recent development, during the initial deployment, Phillips 66 category managers and buyers used Arkestro across refining, midstream, and lubricants operations categories including services. Since launching the program in June, the team has processed approximately $96 million in procurement spend through the platform, identified savings and reduced average cycle times.

Phillips 66 scales predictive procurement after early results.

Sources indicate that the initial deployment demonstrated how predictive procurement can help teams use their own data to move faster and create more competitive outcomes across a broader range of spend. Every awarded event included multiple rounds of supplier competition, with some events completed in fewer than three business days.

It has been revealed that "Our experience working with Arkestro has been extremely positive. The support throughout our initial deployment has been outstanding, and we've made meaningful progress in a relatively short period of time," said Kevin Stein, Director of Strategic Sourcing, Phillips 66.

Sources indicate that "The results have demonstrated the potential to leverage our data to move faster and drive more competitive outcomes across our procurement operations. We're excited to build on that momentum through this expanded partnership and bring those capabilities to more of our business," remarked Scott McRee, Chief Procurement Officer, Phillips 66.

Phillips 66 and Arkestro also worked together during the initial deployment to expand platform capabilities for complex services, including support for labor-rate and burden pricing. These categories can involve multiple pricing variables and service structures that are difficult to evaluate at scale.

The enterprise expansion will extend Arkestro's reach to accelerate strategic sourcing objectives and bolster our impact within capital procurement. The deployment will extend access to all of Phillips 66's procurement organization, enabling them to achieve a consistent predictive procurement process across critical spend.

"Phillips 66 is showing what the power of predictive procurement can look like at enterprise scale," said Rob DeSantis, CEO and co-founder of Arkestro. "By moving from weeks to days and creating stronger competition across more spend, their team is expanding the amount of the business procurement can influence, and we're proud to build on that progress together.".

#41513. What went wrong with Outlook: Microsoft blames ‘thundering herds’ and a bug unnoticed for months

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (824 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Geekwire ↗ Open Full Page

What went wrong with Outlook: Microsoft blames ‘thundering herds’ and a bug unnoticed for months

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (824 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 16, 2026 at 7:31 amNovember 16, 2026 at 7:31 am.
  • Microsoft’s own safety systems helped turn a dormant software flaw into last week’s global Outlook outage, rerouting traffic from failing servers onto healthy ones that had the same problem, until more than 80% of the servers in its Microsoft 365 networking gateway had stopped responding.
  • That phenomenon, known as a cascading failure, is one of the findings in Microsoft’s preliminary report on the outage, released overnight, dissecting the failure that cut off email for people and organizations in more than 70 countries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 16, 2026 at 7:31 amNovember 16, 2026 at 7:31 am.

Microsoft’s own safety systems helped turn a dormant software flaw into last week’s global Outlook outage, rerouting traffic from failing servers onto healthy ones that had the same problem, until more than 80% of the servers in its Microsoft 365 networking gateway had stopped responding.

That phenomenon, known as a cascading failure, is one of the findings in Microsoft’s preliminary report on the outage, released overnight, dissecting the failure that cut off email for people and organizations in more than 70 countries.

According to the report, the attempts to recover were further complicated by a second problem: servers that engineers restarted were immediately overwhelmed by waiting traffic and stopped responding again, a phenomenon known as a “thundering herd.”.

Industry observers note that microsoft says active service disruptions lasted nearly 24 hours. Delayed email continued to be delivered after service returned Friday morning, and the tech giant posted its public all-clear on X late Friday night, nearly 38 hours after the outage began.

The underlying flaw dates to July, when Microsoft began rolling out a fix to the software that handles incoming connections on its networking gateway, the servers that sit in front of Outlook and many other Microsoft 365 services.

It has been revealed that microsoft hasn’t mentioned what the fix was meant to address. It ran worldwide for more than three months without problems, according to the report.

Under heavy load, however, parts of that software could get stuck waiting on one another, using up the servers’ processing power and memory until they froze.

That’s what happened last week. About 15 hours before the outage, Microsoft’s systems automatically moved Teams traffic onto the same servers that handle Outlook email, adding to their load, according to the report. Microsoft called the switch part of normal operations but didn’t say what prompted it.

Complicating matters, nearly 14% of the gateway’s server capacity was already out of service because of an unrelated problem, which also isn’t detailed in the report.

Recent findings suggest that when traffic peaked during the U.S. workday, that was enough to trigger the outage.

Two things stand out as likely areas of scrutiny:.

Sources indicate that microsoft’s testing didn’t catch the bug. Its labs mostly used less powerful machines with fewer processing cores, running a different mix of traffic, while the problem was worst on the newer servers handling real customer load.

The fix also passed through Microsoft’s standard staged rollout, spreading worldwide over several weeks without any sign of trouble, according to the report.

The organization certainly has the means to test on the hardware it actually runs. It spent $45.2 billion on capital expenditures in its most recent quarter, much of it on AI infrastructure.

Industry observers note that the safeguards meant to contain the damage didn’t hold. Walls between regions failed because of what the report calls “a separate problem,” which it doesn’t explain, so the outage went global.

In a recent development, the gateway is made up of thousands of “capacity units” grouped into regions, with walls between them meant to keep a failure in one place. Microsoft also runs a second, independent gateway so services can switch over during a disruption.

Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office apps made that switch, which is why Teams chats and meetings mostly kept working. Exchange couldn’t, “for scale reasons,” as the company put it, so email stayed down.

Microsoft’s own tools added to the problem. Its automated recovery “was not designed” for a fleet that was almost entirely unresponsive, according to the report, and its usual ways of rolling back a bad change couldn’t quickly undo one that was months old.

The firm’s systems automatically shifted traffic from unresponsive servers to healthy ones, and the extra load triggered the same bug on those servers, too. About 10 hours in, engineers turned off some of that automatic rerouting.

Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, posted an abridged version of the report on X late Sunday. “We are deeply sorry for the impact to all our customers and recognize the impact that this has on their normal business & operations,” he wrote.

Lamanna had previewed the findings Friday afternoon, blaming “cascading failures + thundering herds at our network perimeter” for the slow recovery, as GeekWire reported when Microsoft declared the outage over.

It has been revealed that microsoft says it has rolled back the defective code, added server capacity and monitoring, and put new limits on how traffic is redistributed to avoid another cascade. A final report with a full list of repairs is due Nov. 20.

It may also answer the biggest question the preliminary report leaves open: why the walls between regions didn’t stop the outage from spreading worldwide. Microsoft blames that on “a separate issue,” apart from the July bug, but hasn’t mentioned what it was.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yi He, the co-founder of the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, has sparked discussions across the crypto market after urging retail traders to stay calm even as major crypto assets continue to post massive daily losses.

Yi He’s consoling statement has come as crypto traders grow increasingly weary and the prolonged market volatility begins to cause even bigger losses, with Bitcoin retesting $63,000.

In her post, Yi urged investors holding major crypto assets that have been substantially affected by the severe market volatility to remain calm amid the latest market downturn.

She described the ongoing crypto market pullback as ‘temporary’ while assuring spot traders that they have little reason to worry.

Alongside the post, Yi He shared a link to the Binance app showcasing a 30-day asset change of approximately -$101.31 million in her account.

It appears that some investors may have found comfort in Yi He's message as they expressed support, noting that turbulent conditions like these don’t necessarily last long.

However, other commentators have questioned whether wealthy industry figures like Yi He can fully understand the financial pressure facing retail traders at a time like this.

Meanwhile, a loss of 20,000 or 30,000 yuan could wipe out an ordinary investor's savings.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 16, 2026 at 8:31 amNovember 16, 2026 at 8:32 am.
  • Last year, Jeff Bezos asked social media, “Who’d you pick as the next Bond?” Amazon now has its own answer: Robert Pattinson.
  • The 40-year-old Pattinson — best known for “Twilight,” “The Batman” and this summer’s “The Odyssey” — becomes the seventh actor to play 007 in the official film series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 16, 2026 at 8:31 amNovember 16, 2026 at 8:32 am.

Last year, Jeff Bezos asked social media, “Who’d you pick as the next Bond?” Amazon now has its own answer: Robert Pattinson.

The 40-year-old Pattinson — best known for “Twilight,” “The Batman” and this summer’s “The Odyssey” — becomes the seventh actor to play 007 in the official film series. He takes over from Daniel Craig, whose fifth and last Bond film, “No Time to Die,” came out in 2021.

Amazon got a 50% stake in the Bond films when it bought MGM for $8.5 billion in 2022, and it took creative control last year in a joint venture with longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson. Fans and bookmakers had been guessing about Craig’s successor since he mentioned in 2019 he was leaving the role.

Over the years, the rumored contenders included Idris Elba, Tom Hardy, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Tom Holland and Henry Cavill. By the end, there were five finalists. Pattinson beat out Nicholas Hoult, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner after screen tests in London in late October, according to The Latest York Times. Casting director Nina Gold ran the tests, which covered stunts, dialogue and camera presence.

Bond is one of the most valuable properties Amazon got in the MGM deal, its second-largest acquisition ever behind Whole Foods. The franchise has earned nearly $7 billion at the domestic box office, adjusted for inflation, since “Dr. No” in 1962. Now Amazon is running it without the Broccoli family, whose stewardship over six decades built it into one of Hollywood’s biggest moneymakers.

According to recent reports, pattinson’s casting is the most visible move yet in Amazon’s looks for Bond. As the Times noted, the 2025 deal followed years of behind-the-scenes friction over Amazon’s ambitions to expand the Bond universe beyond the films. The Times also pointed out that Amazon has to win over a generation of moviegoers who grew up during the franchise’s long hiatus and gravitated toward superheroes, horror movies and video game adaptations.

In a recent development, amazon is already putting the back catalog to work. Alongside Monday’s announcement, it published a guide to streaming the 007 films on Prime Video.

Identity Confirmed pic.twitter.com/FCU5A9c1wk.

To lead the next film, Amazon brought in producers Amy Pascal, the former Sony Pictures chairwoman, and David Heyman, who produced all eight “Harry Potter” movies. Denis Villeneuve (“Dune”) is directing from an original screenplay by “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight. No release date has been set, and the Times reports that a theatrical release before 2028 is unlikely.

“Today marks a defining moment for our studio and a significant milestone in the history of James Bond,” Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, noted in a statement. Hopkins said Pattinson’s “remarkable range, magnetic screen presence, and quiet intensity make him an exceptional choice” to carry on the 007 legacy.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson said. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.”.

In a recent development, some longtime fans have worried that under Amazon, Bond will lose his distinctly British character and become more corporate and American, the Times reported. Pascal and Heyman, in a joint statement, called the English actor “the perfect Bond for our times.”.

Bezos had yet to weigh back in on social media about Amazon’s pick, but Amazon CEO Andy Jassy did in a LinkedIn post, writing that he was “excited” to have Pattinson in the role, calling him “one of the most versatile actors of his generation, who consistently makes fearless choices, and keeps surprising people with his performances.”.

Fans online were split. Some posted images of Elba or Cavill, calling Pattinson as 007 a “huge miss.” Others said the actor was on a “generational run” right now with the roles he’s landing. Others shared GIFs of Sean Connery, saying there will only ever be one Bond.

It has been revealed that I checked in with my mom, a longtime Bond lover and the biggest movie fan I know. She rapidly responded via text.

Recent findings suggest that “No way … not sexy enough for me,” she wrote of Pattinson. “I really liked Daniel Craig, but Sean Connery has always been a favorite.”.

Sources indicate that deployment services are becoming the real battleground in AI infrastructure as buyers discover that shipping hardware is only half the job. With GPU supply tight and refresh cycles accelerating, neoclouds and enterprises are judging suppliers on how quickly an AI factory actually goes live.

Industry observers note that “It’s not just enough to deliver to the customers. They want it online as swiftly as possible. Time is money,” Thauberger stated.

Thauberger spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how deployment services are driving the race to time to online, how liquid cooling retrofits help older facilities take on modern AI racks and why a one-stop shop makes the blame game go away. (* Disclosure below.).

Sources indicate that customers are leaning on suppliers for far more than boxes. Allocation and deployment services are the two biggest requests Supermicro hears, and its service teams bring systems up, run customer workloads and hand off only once everything is running, Thauberger explained.

“We know that we’re in a constrained environment. There’s no secret on that. So customers are basically asking Supermicro how promptly you can get allocation, how quickly you can bring it online, and how quickly you can have people out on site to deploy those,” Thauberger said.

Older facilities pose another hurdle. Many weren’t designed for the liquid cooling and power density of modern AI racks, so Supermicro offers retrofit options such as sidecars and in-row coolant distribution units, according to Thauberger. The company has also added pre-assembled AI racks to its building-block lineup to shorten installs.

Industry observers note that “We have the largest liquid cooling capacity based in California. We’re a U.S.-headquartered company, and the ability for us to have as much liquid cooling capacity as we have inside the U.S. allows us to deploy to these AI factories quick inside the United States,” Thauberger mentioned.

After 7 Years and 99% Speed Leap, Solana (SOL) Finally Drops Its 'Beta' Label

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Solana has officially removed the "beta" tag from its mainnet's name and introduced the Solana 1.0 standard.
  • "Solana 1.0 marks the network's graduation from 'mainnet beta' to 'mainnet,' retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch," the Solana Foundation said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Solana has officially removed the "beta" tag from its mainnet's name and introduced the Solana 1.0 standard. The switch was confirmed on Nov. 16 at the Breakpoint conference in London.

"Solana 1.0 marks the network's graduation from 'mainnet beta' to 'mainnet,' retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch," the Solana Foundation said.

Solana rolled out on March 16, 2020, and the network had been working under the "mainnet-beta" label for six years and eight months. According to the foundation, the label "never evolved to signal its production status.".

The Solana Foundation coordinated the rollout with the Anza and Firedancer teams. Co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko replied to the announcement on X with three exploding-head emojis.

"For owners, this is the same network, nothing changes. Your SOL, accounts, assets, applications, and transaction history remain the same," the foundation wrote. On Monday, SOL is trading at $71.35.

According to the foundation, two upgrades made the change possible. In October, Solana activated Alpenglow with the Agave 4.3 release, and the time to final confirmation went down by almost 99%, from 12.8 seconds to around 150 milliseconds.

Firedancer, a validator client developed by Jump Crypto independently from Agave, is also now running on the Solana mainnet. Independent implementations "limit the impact of bugs affecting one client, and strengthen network resilience," the foundation stated.

Solana 1.0 also gives the network a shared protocol version, and it does not depend on the version numbers of individual clients such as Agave and Firedancer.

Recent findings suggest that "A shared protocol version lets everyone refer to Solana's evolution without using one client's release number as shorthand for the entire network," the Solana Foundation explained. "Announcing a protocol version does not activate every associated improvement at once.".

Earlier this year, Solana raised the compute limit per block from 60 million to 100 million compute units in May, and the slot time went down from 400 to 200 milliseconds in August. The maximum transaction size also went up from 1,232 to 4,096 bytes.

"Documentation, websites, explorers, and other ecosystem surfaces will progressively reflect the updated designation," the foundation added.

Jazz beat Lakers 109-97 after a 15-0 run ended their 9-game win streak

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Utah beat the 13-3 Lakers 109-97 after a 15-0 fourth-quarter run.
  • The standings said this game would be a mismatch, and it was, with the weaker team on top.
  • According to recent reports, utah did not win this game on a last shot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Utah beat the 13-3 Lakers 109-97 after a 15-0 fourth-quarter run. Three storylines weigh fatigue against the Jazz's own play.

The standings said this game would be a mismatch, and it was, with the weaker team on top. The Jazz, who have won just three games all season, according to AFP, beat the Lakers, one of the strongest teams in the NBA. On paper, Utah should not have been competitive with Los Angeles. That means the story is about what changed on the floor that night, not about which team is better over a full season.

According to recent reports, utah did not win this game on a last shot. The Jazz pulled away and won 109-97, according to AFP, and a double-digit margin leaves little room to call the result a fluke. Why it happened is less clear, and two explanations compete. One holds that the Lakers were too tired to keep up and had nothing left by the end. The other holds that Utah's young players went out and took the game from them. The difference matters to anyone trying to judge either team. If fatigue explains the loss, it is a blip for Los Angeles that a night of rest will fix. If Utah earned the win, the team at the bottom of the league demonstrated something real against one of the teams at the top.

CBS Sports looked at the main threads of the night Utah knocked off a Lakers team that had come in at 13–3, including how badly the Lakers shot and how the Jazz beat both Los Angeles clubs in two days. Those threads hold evidence for the fatigue explanation and for Utah's own play. Neither one settles the game alone, and each deserves a close look, starting with the stretch in which the game turned. Together they lead to a simple question: Was this one strange night for both teams, or the start of something for Utah? The answer will say as much about the Lakers as it does about the Jazz.

Industry observers note that the Jazz stayed even with the Lakers late into the game, and the two teams were tied at 83 before it turned, according to CBS Sports. Utah had kept pace with one of the league's strongest teams into the closing stretch. From that tie, Utah scored 15 points in a row. A level game became a Utah game in a single stretch. The upset came down to that run, not to an advantage Utah built slowly across four quarters. Any explanation for the result has to account for those minutes.

Recent findings suggest that if fatigue were the whole story, the points could have come from any Utah player against a slowing Lakers defense. Instead, two Utah players each scored heavily in the closing quarter. Ace Bailey scored 10 fourth-quarter points for the Jazz, and Keyonte George added 9 more. Two players attacking as the game turned looks more like a team taking control of a close game than one player's lucky streak, and it points toward Utah winning with its own play. Still, a long run of unanswered Utah points could also mean the Lakers had run out of energy, and the scoring alone does not settle the question.

The fourth quarter shows Utah was ready to take the game. Whether the Lakers gave it away is a question about their shooting.

The Lakers shot worse against Utah than in any other game this season. They made 38.2% of their shots, their lowest mark of the year, according to CBS Sports, and hit just 27.3% of their three-pointers. The schedule offers the easiest explanation. The Lakers were playing for the second night in a row, and the first of those games went to overtime. Tired players commonly miss jump shots, and the Lakers missed a great many of them. If fatigue is the whole story, the loss says little about either team, and the Lakers can move on from it.

Sources indicate that fatigue should affect a whole roster, but much of this slump came from one player. Lakers star Luka Doncic went 2-of-12 from three-point range, while the team as a whole went 9-of-33 from deep, according to Bleacher Report. His misses made up a large share of the Lakers' failed three-point attempts that night. That pattern fits a Utah defense focused on stopping one player at least as well as it fits a tired team. How much credit Utah deserves remains an open question.

Doncic also lost the ball far more often than usual. Only one game this season saw him turn it over more than the nine times he did against Utah, according to Bleacher Report. Fatigue commonly explains missed jump shots, but a high turnover count points at least partly to the defenders guarding him. Doncic himself did not mention the schedule. "Honestly, I just got to do way better than this," Doncic said. The player with the most reason to cite a second game in two nights blamed his own play instead.

That weakens the fatigue explanation without ruling it out, and whether Utah did more than catch a tired team is a question for the rest of the week.

Sources indicate that utah's win over the Lakers came a day after a win over the city's other NBA team, which gave the Jazz victories against both Los Angeles opponents in two days, according to CBS Sports. Two Utah wins over two Los Angeles opponents in two days turn one odd result into a pattern that needs an explanation. The sweep also matched the worst form in this game against the best. The Jazz had won once in their first 14 games. The loss ended a nine-game Lakers winning streak, according to AFP. A rout of a slumping rival could be shrugged off, but ending a streak that long is harder to dismiss as luck.

In a recent development, the Lakers were not the only team playing for a second straight night. Utah's win over the other Los Angeles team came the evening before, so the Jazz also had a game behind them when they pulled away late. Rest makes a weaker explanation when the winning team was also playing its second game in two nights, even if the Lakers carried the heavier load. That doesn't erase the fatigue explanation, but it shrinks it, and it leaves room for the other reading: Utah's young players took the game rather than waiting for the Lakers to give it away.

Two wins still don't make a turnaround. Even after the sweep, Utah sits at 3–13, and two wins can't undo what the first weeks of the season did to that record, so this still reads as an upset. The next test comes on November 23, when the Jazz and Lakers meet again before this result has time to fade.

If Utah wins again in a game where the Lakers can't blame the schedule, the case that its young players are taking games gains ground; if the Lakers win comfortably, the sweep will look like two lucky nights.

  • According to recent reports, A Harvard-led study estimates that electricity use at 403 U.S.
  • Industry observers note that the research examined some of the nation’s largest and most powerful data center facilities operating between May 2024 and April 2025.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 16, 2026 at 10:01 amNovember 17, 2026 at 3:48 pm.

According to recent reports, A Harvard-led study estimates that electricity use at 403 U.S. hyperscale data centers was equal to roughly 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions — a volume roughly comparable to Denmark’s carbon footprint.

Industry observers note that the research examined some of the nation’s largest and most powerful data center facilities operating between May 2024 and April 2025. Together, those facilities accounted for an estimated 1.8% of total U.S. electricity consumption.

“What we’re seeing is already striking, but it’s only a snapshot of a rapidly expanding industry,” Gianluca Guidi, the study’s lead author and a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Biostatistics at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, noted in a statement.

In a recent development, guidi noted that the data center boom has continued since the study period ended. “That means the electricity use and carbon footprint we’re reporting could already be substantially larger now in 2026.”.

The research, published in the journal Nature Sustainability and explored in an associated website, comes amid growing pushback and concerns about the facilities’ impacts on electric bills, water consumption, noise and carbon emissions.

Sources indicate that in the Pacific Northwest, government officials are enacting moratoriums and exploring legislation to regulate data center development. Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek in October directed a state agency to pause processing and issuing permits for latest and expanding data centers until July 2027. In Washington, state Rep. Beth Doglio, D-Olympia, will propose data center rules in the legislative session that starts in January.

Hyperscale sites handle massive computing workloads and data storage, supporting operations including large language model training and AI deployment.

The researchers found that Oregon ranked second in electricity used by hyperscale data centers in the study, consuming about half as much as those in Virginia. Given Oregon’s access to clean hydropower, the state ranked sixth in carbon dioxide emissions attributed to the facilities’ electricity use. The publication highlighted data from the top 10 states for energy use, which does not include Washington.

Nationwide, roughly 54% of the electricity attributed to the facilities came from fossil fuels, primarily natural gas and coal. The estimates were based on regional power generation mixes, not individual operators’ clean energy purchases.

The study did not break out energy use by data center operator. Amazon, Microsoft and Google have the largest data center footprints worldwide and account for 57% of hyperscale data center capacity, according to Synergy Research Group.

All three have aggressive carbon reduction targets. While their emissions have all increased in recent years, the companies say they remain committed to their goals. Microsoft and Amazon point to their support for newly introduced clean power projects and investments in low-carbon building materials for the facilities as positive steps towards reductions.

“We continue to really be focused around carbon negativity by 2030,” Melanie Nakagawa, Microsoft’s chief sustainability officer, told GeekWire in July.

Kara Hurst, Amazon’s chief sustainability officer, acknowledged that it will be difficult for the company to reach its target of net-zero emissions by 2040.

“So that is a real challenge,” Hurst said in September, “and we’re here to meet the moment. I’m not saying that it’s going to be easy, and I’m not saying it’s going to be linear. But we’re going to put everything we have behind that.”.

At the same time, both tech giants are pursuing projects involving fossil fuel energy in Texas. Microsoft in June signed a 20-year deal to purchase power from a natural gas facility slated to come online in 2028. Amazon has agreed to become the anchor tenant of a massive planned data center campus with proposed natural gas and nuclear power generation, according to the Financial Times.

“Assessing the Carbon Emissions and Energy Consumption of US Hyperscale Data Centers” published in Nature Sustainability and researchers from the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, University of Pisa, IMT School of Advanced Studies, Aurora Energy Research, Environmental Systems Research Institute, Baxtel and UCLA Fielding School of Public Health.

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Another day, another security scare. This time, Etherscan is warning users after detecting attempts to gain unauthorized access to its customer support system. But the timing could hardly be worse for an industry already dealing with a growing list of cyberattacks.

The warning comes just days after hackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely, injecting malicious code into websites operated by 178 organizations. The affected names included HSBC, BBC, Ledger, IKEA, Salesforce, Zoom, and CNN.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, crypto platforms have faced separate attacks involving compromised API keys, protocol vulnerabilities, and stolen customer information. Traditional banking has not escaped either, with a French bank recently losing approximately €100 million to hackers.

So what kind of security era are we entering? The problem is no longer confined to crypto exchanges or experimental DeFi protocols. Banks, technology companies, payment providers and blockchain businesses are increasingly exposed to the same interconnected digital infrastructure.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

Etherscan disclosed earlier today that attackers had attempted to gain unauthorized access to its Freshworks customer support and ticketing system. The firm is investigating and has introduced precautionary measures. It has not confirmed that customer records were successfully accessed, but warned users about suspicious support communications, unexpected links, and requests for sensitive information.

Security Notice: Reminder Regarding Etherscan Support CommunicationsEarlier today, we detected attempts to gain unauthorized access to our customer support and ticketing system (Freshworks).We are currently investigating the situation and taking precautionary measures.In….

Sources indicate that the concern is particularly relevant because support impersonation remains an effective way to steal people’ crypto and money. An attacker posing as an Etherscan representative could exploit a user’s existing support request to make a phishing message appear legitimate.

In a recent development, but Etherscan is hardly the only name facing security questions this week. Just two days ago, hackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely’s Web Experimentation signup process. They injected malicious JavaScript into customer projects, allowing the code to run on websites using the affected software.

Optimizely confirmed the vulnerability and mentioned it had removed the injected code and fixed the flaw. Its November 17 incident report said the unauthorized party exploited the signup process rather than stealing customer administrator passwords.

The financial damage remains unclear. It is reported that investigators could not establish how many visitors were affected or whether the attempted thefts succeeded.

Industry observers note that the uncomfortable takeaway is that attackers did not need to breach 178 separate companies. They exploited one software provider whose code was embedded across hundreds of websites.

In a recent development, crypto’s security problems extend beyond Etherscan and the Optimizely incident. DeFiLlama’s hack tracker recorded several attacks during the week, including a $10.39 million incident involving Lighter Perps on November 16. The attacker exploited a compromised trader API key, enabling unauthorized withdrawals.

Sources indicate that lighter said its protocol and smart contracts were not compromised. It temporarily suspended withdrawals and activated Guardian mode to prevent further unauthorized activity.

It has been revealed that another incident hit MORE Markets, where an attacker exploited a lending mechanism to drain approximately $308,000 in WFLOW. B18 TimeBank also suffered an exploit on November 17, losing $404,540 in USDC through its reward voucher redemption mechanism.

Industry observers note that these incidents show different weaknesses across crypto infrastructure. Not every loss comes from a broken smart contract. Compromised credentials, vulnerable applications and flawed authorization mechanisms can be equally damaging.

Traditional finance faces its own problems. French lender Crédit Mutuel Arkéa disclosed a cyber heist earlier in November, with hackers stealing approximately €100 million through fraudulent transactions originating from the bank’s own accounts. The bank mentioned customer assets were not affected, although some transactions were temporarily suspended.

Deutsche Bank also made headlines on November 17 after confidential internal documents surfaced through an international journalistic investigation. It was a document leak, not a confirmed breach of its current banking systems.

Sources indicate that deutsche Bank said security testing found no indication that its current IT environment, account information, login credentials, or payment data had been compromised. Still, the leak could have wider geopolitical repercussions.

Banking institutions are not immune to major security incidents simply because they operate under traditional financial regulations.

In a recent development, crypto has suffered enormous losses. The October Binance incident alone involved $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, making it one of the largest cryptocurrency heists on record. Yet, traditional finance also faces attacks involving payment infrastructure, third-party service providers, and internal transaction systems.

The Optimizely incident is particularly revealing. Both HSBC and Ledger appeared among the affected organizations. The vulnerability did not care whether visitors were interacting with a traditional financial institution or a crypto manufacturer.

In a recent development, neither system offers complete protection. The real question is whether companies can secure the increasingly complex infrastructure connecting their services. A single compromised vendor can expose hundreds of organizations, while one stolen credential can bypass otherwise sophisticated security systems.

According to recent reports, crypto owners have every reason to demand stronger protections. But traditional banking customers should not mistake regulation and familiar branding for immunity.

With Etherscan investigating attempted unauthorized access, the data provider is now joining the growing list of companies dealing with security incidents.
